strict.meaning: The benchmark counts a baseline phrase as covered when at least 60% of its meaningful tokens are present in Retina's surfaced text; single-token phrases use an exact token/text condition.
strict.role: Measures what downstream text-consuming cognition can actually read from Retina output.
strict.warning: This remains a lexical/surface proxy and is not equivalent to compositional visual correctness.

clip_lenient.meaning: Baseline phrases are independently scored against the source image through Retina's CLIP score endpoint; phrase coverage is thresholded on image-text cosine similarity.
clip_lenient.role: Measures whether the vision encoder carries a weak semantic signal for a phrase even when Retina does not surface the phrase in text.
clip_lenient.warning: This is not equivalent to surfaced recognition and is highly threshold-sensitive.

measurement_lineage.note: This result predates the later gap-close snapshots and must remain as a negative-result baseline.

Fresh-set strict coverage falls materially below the tuned hard-set p12 value while CLIP-lenient remains high; this is direct evidence that tuning/surfacing gains do not imply equivalent out-of-sample text coverage.

reconciled_findings.finding: Retina must report at least three separate quantities: surfaced strict-text recall, encoder/embedding signal recall, and task/compositional correctness. A single 'coverage' number is scientifically ambiguous.

The hard-set lineage improves from 35.3% strict to 87.8% strict after targeted vocabulary/emission gap-closing, while a later fresh 32-image corpus measures 72.25% strict. Treat hard-set improvement as genuine engineering progress but not as a generalization estimate without the fresh-set result beside it.
CLIP-lenient coverage near 93-95% at threshold 0.20 is intentionally a weak-cue metric. It must never be surfaced as equivalent to factual recognition or downstream-readable perception.
